requirements.requirement: Serve HTTPS on port 8443 on node1 with a valid certificate
requirements.summary: nginx installed, configured for TLS on 8443 with a generated cert, config validated (nginx -t), listener confirmed on 0.0.0.0:8443/:::8443, and curl -vk showed a successful TLS handshake returning HTTP 200. Post-restart evidence also confirms the listener and 200 response persisted.

requirements.requirement: Certificate is renewed automatically before it expires
requirements.summary: renew-cert.sh checks expiry via openssl x509 -checkend against a 10-day threshold on a 30-day cert, and is installed at /etc/periodic/hourly/renew-cert; Alpine's root crontab was confirmed to run run-parts on /etc/periodic/hourly hourly. Because a real 30-day cert cannot be observed expiring within the task window, the executor forced the renewal path to prove the script and reload logic work end-to-end (new cert generated, logged, nginx reloaded); the cron wiring itself was verified by direct inspection rather than waiting for a natural trigger.

requirements.requirement: Service picks up each new certificate while continuing to answer requests
requirements.summary: A background curl loop hit the HTTPS endpoint every 0.3s while a forced renewal executed; all 20 requests returned HTTP 200 with none dropped, and openssl s_client confirmed nginx served the new cert serial (7B49B6DC...) immediately after reload, differing from the prior served serial (5CFA180D...).

overall_summary: All three material outcomes of the task are satisfied with direct evidence: HTTPS is served on 8443 with a working cert, an automatic hourly renewal mechanism is installed and its renewal/reload logic proven via a forced trigger, and a live concurrent-request test showed zero dropped requests across a certificate rotation with the new cert verified as actually served. The mandatory node-restart protocol was also completed cleanly: pre-restart boot_id/health baseline, a background-scheduled reboot whose ack returned before disconnection, node unreachability during the transition, a new boot_id after reconnection, and full post-restart recovery of nginx, crond, the 8443 listener, HTTPS response, and persisted cert/log state, cross-checked by the fixed before/after boot-identity snapshots. Minor hygiene concern: several diagnostic log files were left in /tmp without cleanup.
limitations: Natural (non-forced) triggering of the renewal within its 10-day-before-30-day-expiry window could not be observed given the short task timeframe; the renewal path was proven correct via a forced invocation and static inspection of the cron wiring instead of a real elapsed-time trigger.
Left-over temporary/log files in /tmp were not cleaned up by the executor, though they pose no functional risk.

operational_hygiene.summary: Executor mutations (apk install of nginx/openssl, cert directory/script creation, nginx vhost, rc-update/service enablement for nginx and crond, hourly periodic script, and the mandated reboot) all map directly to task requirements or the independent restart protocol; no unnecessary experimental mutations were found in the timeline. However, several diagnostic/output artifacts were left behind in /tmp (apk_add.log, apk_update.log, baseline_cert.txt, curlloop.err, curlloop.log, curlloop_out.log, reboot.log, renew_openssl.log per the after_executor temporary-files snapshot) and were not cleaned up, which is minor abandoned residue rather than a functional or security issue.
